title: Cholera Surge in Khartoum — 2,500 Cases in Three Weeks; Over 1 Million Children at Risk
detail: MSF reported on May 26, 2026 that cholera is spreading rapidly in Khartoum, with 2,500 cases recorded in just three weeks. The Khartoum Ministry of Health separately reported 633 cases and 24 deaths on May 23 alone. Over 1 million children in Khartoum are at risk of cholera infection, according to health authorities. The outbreak is driven by the near-total destruction of Khartoum's water and sanitation infrastructure during two years of urban combat: 80% of water supply facilities were damaged or destroyed, sewage treatment has collapsed, and millions displaced by the war are returning to neighborhoods without functioning services. One year after SAF expelled RSF from Khartoum, the city faces simultaneous crises: cholera, a $3 billion electricity infrastructure deficit, and collapsed health services. The cholera outbreak compounds Sudan's broader public health collapse — 37% of health facilities nationwide are non-functional, and RSF drone attacks have struck 12+ healthcare facilities since January 2026. WHO and MSF are conducting emergency response operations in affected neighborhoods. The outbreak reflects the toll of infrastructure devastation after 18 months of urban combat in one of Africa's largest cities.

media.caption: Cholera spreads rapidly in Khartoum in May 2026: 2,500 cases in three weeks, 24 deaths May 23 alone, and 1 million+ children at risk amid collapsed water and sanitation infrastructure.

title: SAF Retakes Five Towns in Blue Nile's Qaysan District — RSF/SPLM-N Forces Pushed Toward Ethiopian Border
detail: Sudanese Armed Forces retook Abdaqla, Adi, Washimbu, Um Shanqar, and Kinshinkaru in Qaysan district, Blue Nile State on May 26, 2026, forcing RSF and allied SPLM-N (al-Hilu) forces to retreat toward the Ethiopian border. The advance is part of SAF's sustained Blue Nile offensive that has progressively rolled back the RSF-SPLM-N coalition since its capture of Kurmuk on March 23, 2026. The SAF counteroffensive in Blue Nile follows a coordinated multi-front strategy: SAF recaptured Al-Barka near Kurmuk (May 24), Kern Kern and Doukan (May 18), and Khor Hasan (May 15) in rapid succession throughout May. The Qaysan gains push the front line southeast toward the Ethiopian border, compressing the RSF-SPLM-N Blue Nile pocket and threatening to cut the corridor through which SPLM-N fighters stage from Ethiopia. Qaysan district was among the areas seized during the RSF-SPLM-N push that also triggered 50,000+ Blue Nile civilian displacements and a 4,000+ Ethiopian border refugee flow in March 2026. The SAF-aligned Savanna Movement also announced its intention to fight alongside SAF forces in Blue Nile on May 15, expanding the coalition pushing against the RSF-SPLM-N alliance. IOM documented 73,000+ newly displaced people fleeing into Ed Damazin (Blue Nile capital) following the March RSF-SPLM-N offensive; retaking Qaysan district aims to enable eventual civilian return.

title: IOM Documents 46,000 Newly Displaced in West Kordofan During May 2026
detail: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) documented approximately 46,000 people newly displaced in West Kordofan State during May 2026 alone, driven by escalating insecurity and continued drone strikes on civilian-populated towns. West Kordofan — which includes the state capital El Fula and towns such as Ghubaysh (hit by a drone strike killing 28 on May 19) and Abu Zaima — has seen intensifying violence as SAF and RSF contest territory along the Kordofan-Darfur corridor. This figure represents one month's displacement in a single state and underscores the cascading humanitarian impact of continued fighting even as SAF has achieved significant military gains in the broader theater. The May displacement figure for West Kordofan alone approaches the scale of the entire Blue Nile crisis following the March 2026 Kurmuk offensive (50,000+). Sudan's total displacement reached 14 million+ as of mid-May 2026; the UN appeals for Sudan are only approximately 20% funded. IOM continues to document displacement movements across Sudan's conflict zones.
